decisions: LeasedAtomicIngestCommitter wraps the T034 AtomicIngestCommitter boundary and acquires one lease derived from all coverage records before publishing either staged object or catalog state.
A commit must contain coverage records for exactly one asset-class, symbol, and session date, preventing a mixed batch from sharing an ambiguous lock scope.
Lease and LeaseProvider are injectable protocols; local tests use a blocking fake to prove two concurrent writers reach the backend commit serially and that failures still release the scope.

AzureBlobLeaseProvider uses the T027 token-credential pattern, creates a deterministic lock blob without overwriting it, and delegates renewal and release through the acquired ID-bound BlobLeaseClient.
AzureBlobLease makes release idempotent and rejects renewal after release; the lock blob remains for subsequent writers to lease.
limitations: All focused Azure tests use local SDK-shaped fakes; no live Azure request, credential, network access, or Azure mutation was used.
The Azure adapter reports lease-acquisition failures to the caller for normal job retry handling rather than adding an unbounded polling loop.
The shared worktree contains unrelated user changes and untracked files; none were modified, staged, reverted, or committed by T062.
No MyPy run was performed; repository tooling uses Ruff and ty.
